title: String concatenation
starter_code:
first_name = "Ada"
last_name = "Lovelace"
# Create full_name and print it
solution_code:
first_name = "Ada"
last_name = "Lovelace"
full_name = first_name + " " + last_name
print(full_name)
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_full_name():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == 'Ada Lovelace\n', f"Expected Ada Lovelace, got {output!r}"

title: Use an f-string
instruction: Use an f-string to print Tokyo population.
starter_code:
city = "Tokyo"
population = 37_000_000
# Print using an f-string
solution_code:
city = "Tokyo"
population = 37_000_000
print(f"{city} has a population of {population}.")
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_fstring_population():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == 'Tokyo has a population of 37000000.\n', f"Expected Tokyo population string, got {output!r}"

title: Upper and lower case
instruction: Convert text to uppercase, then lowercase, print each.
starter_code:
text = "PyThOn Is AwEsOmE"
# Convert to upper and lower
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_upper_and_lower():

    sys.stdout = captured

title: Check string length
instruction: Print len(quote), then check if "mind" is in quote.
starter_code:
quote = "The mind is everything. What you think you become."
# Print length, then check if "mind" is in quote
solution_code:
quote = "The mind is everything. What you think you become."
print(len(quote))
print("mind" in quote)
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_length_and_contains():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == '50\nTrue\n', f"Expected length 50 then True, got {output!r}"
